title: Empowerment: The Drive for Control
excerpt: In the absence of specific physiological deficits or external rewards, biological agents do not simply idle; they actively restructure their environment to increase the number of future states they can reliably access. This drive is formalized as empowerment .
html:
In the absence of specific physiological deficits or external rewards, biological agents do not simply idle; they actively restructure their environment to increase the number of future states they can reliably access. This drive is formalized as empowerment 1, 2. Unlike the drive for compression (which seeks to understand the world), empowerment seeks to dominate the causal dynamics of the world. It operationalizes the intuition that a "good" state is not just a safe one, but one that offers the agent the maximum number of distinct, controllable futures–effectively, a drive to maximize the channel capacity of the actuator-to-sensor loop.

Formally, empowerment is defined using information theory. The agent treats the environment as a communication channel: its actions are the "transmitted signal" and the resulting sensory changes are the "received signal." An agent is empowered when its actions have a high mutual information with future sensory states–meaning different actions lead to reliably distinguishable outcomes. For a current state sts_t, a sequence of kk actions ak:t+ka_{k:t+k}, and the resulting future state st+ks_{t+k}, empowerment is the maximum possible mutual information achievable by an optimal policy: A foundational paper illustrates empowerment as an action–sensation channel (Figure) 6. A computational study compares empowerment and expected-free-energy agents (Figure) 7.

ℰ(st)=maxp(a)I(At:t+k;St+k|st)=maxp(a)(H(St+k|st)−H(St+k|st,At:t+k))\begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(s_t) = \max_{p(a)} I(A_{t:t+k} ; S_{t+k} | s_t) = \max_{p(a)} \left( H(S_{t+k}|s_t) - H(S_{t+k}|s_t, A_{t:t+k}) \right) \end{equation}

This equation reveals two critical components of control. To maximize , the agent must maximize H(St+k|st)H(S_{t+k}|s_t) (the diversity of reachable futures) while minimizing H(St+k|st,At:t+k)H(S_{t+k}|s_t,A_{t:t+k}) (the uncertainty of an outcome given a specific action). In plain English: "I want to be in a position where I can make many different things happen (high potential entropy), but where I know exactly which action causes which result (low conditional entropy/noise)."

This makes empowerment a clean formalization of an intrinsic motivation for option value: an organism can pursue high-empowerment states without specifying any particular external goal, because high controllability is a prerequisite for all future goal satisfaction. In the empowerment literature, this is explicitly framed as a pseudo-utility that induces a preference for "states that allow the agent to change its future," and the limiting case of vanishing empowerment aligns with being effectively unable to act (the control channel degenerates) 3. While the functional logic of empowerment is to maximize future optionality, its biological realization appears as a primitive drive for causal efficacy–an "effectance" motive that motivates exploration even in the absence of extrinsic payoff 4, 5; "keeping options open" is the evolutionary why, but "dominating causal dynamics" is the behavioral how.
